title: Introduction & Week 12 (Progress 30 of 30) Overview
text: Hi, I am Varun and this video is about week 12 of Project Medavi, building all the remaining physics videos, smoothing the new intro and outro, and publishing five more shorts. On October 17th, I asked for every remaining video as soon as possible. The count turned out to be 31 storyboards, not 29. So, 21 concepts were left. Claude code ran four parallel agents from one shared brief and by October 18th all 30 concepts were built. I approved portrait at 30 frames per second since 60 was wasted and GPU encodes for 4K. title: Scaling Video Builds with 4 Parallel Claude Code Agents
text: And never mixed within one video. Running everything at once crashed the Linux side several times. So renders, narration, and encodes got locks that allow one of each at a time. Then an API rate limit stopped all four agents, and they were resumed from their saved work. Later in the week, I said the intro and outro felt abrupt, then that the intro was disjointed. Claude Code measured the frames and audio and found the questions starting while the logo still faded, and the intro's sound cut off. A new recipe holds the logo, fades the sound, and dissolves through white. 23 shorts were restitched. Five shorts went live with descriptions written for all 24 that were waiting. text: Repo, but the first push hung for 24 minutes, waiting for a GitHub login that this clone doesn't have. So, it was pushed once with the stored Windows login. From six concepts built at the end of September to nine on October 15th to all 30 by October 18th. Claude Code built the 30 concepts, ran the locks, tested GPU narration, and corrected physics in the story boards like orbit energy where the storyboard had the burn backwards. I decided the speedups, gave the intro feedback, and published the shorts. The takeaway, parallel work needs locks.
